newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen slipping further in near-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen slipping further in near-term.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE coffee futures should continue to feel some pressure in the near-term after a weak close near session lows on Tuesday, technical analysts said.
Mathematically, July was called to open down about $200 but traders said the opening could actually range anywhere between down $70 and $200 because of coffee's extreme volatility.

Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden, said robusta prices would continue following New York prices lower in the near-term. New York ended weak on Tuesday, with July down 35.35 at 217.95 cents per pound and September down 26.85 at 196.75. Both were just off session lows.
September robustas closed on session lows after trading an outside day on Tuesday, which should indicate a reversal of the previous few days of gains.

Initial September support rests at $1,772, the 61.8-percent retracement of the bull run dating back to January, Haylor said. Below that, support rests near $1,710. He said the narrower range from February to May between about $1,550 and $1,700 would be considered an entire base of support.

If coffee tests the upside, Haylor sees September resistance between $1,840 and $1,850. Above that, $2,000 should contain further upside moves in the near-term, he said. --Medora Lee, London newsroom +44 171 542 8072
